name: Stocks in play: relative-volume ranked 5-minute opening range breakout
rule: Universe: liquid NSE stocks, prev_close>=100, ATR14/price>=1%. At 09:20 compute RVOL5 = volume(09:15-09:19)/mean of the same window over the prior 14 sessions. Keep RVOL5>=1; take top N by RVOL5. If first 5-min candle close>open place buy-stop at its high; if close<open sell-stop at its low; skip doji. Stop k*ATR14 from entry. Exit 15:10. Risk 1% of equity per trade; total leverage cap 5x.
instruments: NSE cash equities, intraday (MIS), long and short
reported_performance: US stocks 2016-2023, net of $0.0035/share, no slippage model: top 20 by relative volume Sharpe 2.81, IRR 41.6%, max drawdown 12%; same entry without the volume filter Sharpe 0.48, IRR 3.2%. Average per trade -0.02R below 100% relative volume, +0.08R above, +0.38R above 3000%. Replication covers 2016 only (Sharpe 2.4).
feasibility_reason: Cash MIS at 5x allows 2-3 positions of Rs 1.5-2.5 lakh, but a 0.1*ATR stop is about 0.25% of price and an Indian round trip costs about 0.13% with slippage, roughly 0.5R against a published average edge of 0.08R. Needs a wider stop or only extreme relative volume.

name: Opening gap fade (ordinary gap, no catalyst)
rule: At 09:15 flag stocks opening above prev high or below prev low with 0.2%<=|gap|<=3%, not a results day. At 09:20 require RVOL5<1.5 and first 5-min candle closing toward the prior range. Enter against the gap (short gap-up, long gap-down). Target prior day high (gap-up) or low (gap-down). Stop 0.5*ATR14 beyond the opening-range extreme. Time exit 12:30, else 15:10.
instruments: NSE cash equities, intraday (MIS), long and short
reported_performance: S&P 500 members, two years to Oct 2010, 125,811 stock-days: 76% of opening gaps traded back into the prior day's range the same day, 70% for gaps above 0.2%, only 9.6% for gaps beyond 5%. Hit rates only; no profit, stop or cost figures.
feasibility_reason: Runs in cash MIS in both directions, but the target is the gap itself (0.4-1%), so a 0.13-0.27% round trip takes a third or more of the gross, and the losers are news gaps that do not fill.

name: Gap and go: large gap with abnormal opening volume
rule: Select stocks with |gap|>=max(2%, ATR14/price) and RVOL5>=2. Trade only in the gap direction: stop-entry at the 5-min opening-range extreme, valid to 11:00. Stop at the opposite end of the opening range, capped at 0.5*ATR14. Exit 15:10. Max 2 positions. Skip the day if over 20% of the universe gapped the same way by more than 1%.
instruments: NSE cash equities, intraday (MIS), long and short
reported_performance: No direct test found. Indirect: US gaps beyond 5% filled only 9.6% of the time (2008-2010); high relative-volume breakouts averaged +0.38R at over 30x volume (US 2016-2023). Against: gap continuation on Micro Nasdaq futures failed walk-forward validation, 2021-2025 (T=1.46, year-unstable).
feasibility_reason: One or two cash MIS positions a day at most; few signals a month in a 200-stock universe. Edge unproven for India.

name: Narrow range (NR4/NR7) and inside day breakout
rule: After the close flag stocks whose daily range is the smallest of the last 7 sessions (NR7); variants NR4, inside day, NR7 plus inside day. Next session place buy-stop at pattern-day high and sell-stop at pattern-day low; first trigger only, valid to 13:00. Stop at the other side of the pattern range or 0.5*ATR14, whichever is nearer. Exit 15:10. Variant: sell side only.
instruments: NSE cash equities, intraday (MIS), long and short
holding_period: intraday; variants next day and 5 days in the source
reported_performance: Indian F&O stocks from 2015, NR7 plus inside bar, 2,238 signals, no costs, units undefined: same-day exit averaged +124 per buy signal (546 wins, 611 losses) and +473 per sell signal (642 wins, 484 losses). US stocks 1990-2013: only upward breakouts in bull markets were profitable ($78.79 per trade, 57% wins).
feasibility_reason: Selection needs only daily bars; trades are cash MIS. The narrow pattern range makes stops tight, so cost per unit of risk is high.

name: Volatility and range-expansion universe filter
rule: Each morning rank the universe by ATR14/prev_close. Allow trend-following intraday entries only in stocks with ATRpct>=min_atr_pct, or in the top third by ATRpct. Optional: require the previous day's true range>=1.5*ATR14 (range expansion) or the widest range of the last 7 days. Apply as an on/off filter to every base strategy and compare results with and without it.
instruments: filter applied to NSE cash equities
reported_performance: US 2016 replication: ATR floors from $0 to $2 all gave Sharpe 1.5-2.7, and an ATR>1% of price filter gave 2.24, so the level is not critical. Nifty index 30-minute breakout, Jul 2017-Mar 2026, no costs: wide opening-range days +30.3% versus tiny-range days +18.6%.
feasibility_reason: A filter; costs nothing to run. Volatility is needed for moves large enough to cover a 0.07-0.27% round trip, but it gives no direction.

name: Intraday relative strength versus NIFTY and sector
rule: At T compute RS = stock return since prev_close minus beta*NIFTY return since prev_close (60-day beta). If NIFTY return>0 buy top k by RS that are above session VWAP and above the 30-min opening-range high; if <0 short bottom k below VWAP and below the 30-min range low. Optional: the stock's sector must rank top or bottom two by mean RS. Stop VWAP cross or 0.5*ATR14. Exit 15:10.
instruments: NSE cash equities, intraday (MIS), long and short
reported_performance: No rigorous test found in any market. Related only: US stocks with high past-month intraday returns keep earning high intraday returns (+2.19% a month decile spread, 1993-2013); index-level momentum into the close.
feasibility_reason: Two cash MIS positions of Rs 1.5-3 lakh keep the round trip near 0.05-0.07%. Needs a sector map (other). Edge untested.

name: Index direction gate (market intraday momentum)
rule: r_open = NIFTY(09:45)/NIFTY prev_close-1. If |r_open|>=0.3% allow only stock trades in that direction today; else both. Late variant: at 14:40 if NIFTY return since prev_close is positive buy (negative: short) the 2 stocks with the largest beta-adjusted same-direction return; exit 15:10.
instruments: filter on NSE cash equities; late variant trades 2 stocks (MIS)
holding_period: gate: all day; late variant 30 minutes
reported_performance: S&P 500 ETF 1993-2013: first half-hour return from the prior close predicts the last half-hour return, stronger on volatile and high-volume days; an earlier 1999-2012 version reported R-squared 2% and 6.34% a year. Over 60 futures 1974-2020 show the same. The overnight-return variant disappears out of sample. Not tested as a stock filter.
feasibility_reason: The gate is free. The late variant earns a half-hour move that is small against a 0.07% round trip, and our 15:10 exit misses the true last half hour.

name: Same-time-of-day continuation (intraday periodicity)
rule: Split 09:15-15:15 into 12 half-hour intervals. For stock s and interval j, score = mean return of s in interval j over the previous 20 sessions. Standalone: in interval j go long the top decile and short the bottom decile by score, exit at interval end. Practical: use the score sign only to time entries of other strategies.
instruments: NSE cash equities, intraday (MIS), long and short
reported_performance: US stocks (Journal of Finance 2010): return continuation at half-hour intervals that are exact multiples of a day, lasting at least 40 days; authors' practical claim is a saving equal to the effective spread from timing trades. Abstract only read; no return figure quoted.
feasibility_reason: Up to 12 round trips a day per name at 0.07-0.27% each; the effect is of spread size. Only usable as an entry-timing tie-breaker.

name: Intraday-return persistence (overnight versus intraday tug of war)
rule: Daily: ID21 = product(close/open)-1 and ON21 = product(open/prev_close)-1 over the last 21 sessions. Long list = top decile by ID21; short list = bottom decile by ID21 (variant: sort on ON21, inverted). Direct test: buy the long list at the open, sell at the close; short the short list at the open, cover at the close. Practical: use the lists as a direction filter for other intraday strategies.
instruments: NSE cash equities, intraday (MIS), long and short
reported_performance: US 1993-2013, value-weighted deciles: past-month intraday winners minus losers earn +2.19% a month intraday (t=6.72) and -1.77% overnight; past-month overnight winners minus losers earn -3.24% a month intraday (t=-9.34). Nine other markets: +2.80% a month intraday continuation. Gross, at opening prints. India not in the sample.
feasibility_reason: Traded directly it needs about 21 round trips a month per name, 1.5-2.7% a month in charges, which consumes the gross spread. Usable as a direction filter.

name: High-volume return premium (yesterday's volume shock)
rule: At the close flag stocks whose traded value today ranks in the top 5 of the last 50 sessions and |close-to-close return|<1.5%, price>=50. Next session: long-only watchlist; enter on a break of the 15-min opening-range high with RVOL5>=1; stop 0.5*ATR14; exit 15:10. Also measure plain open-to-close and close-to-close returns after the flag.
instruments: NSE cash equities, long only (MIS)
holding_period: intraday; source effect is 1 to 20 days
reported_performance: NYSE Aug 1963-Dec 1996: high-minus-low volume portfolios earned 0.35% (1 day) to 0.94% (20 days) per dollar long in small stocks and 0.12% to 0.50% in large stocks; stronger when the volume shock came without an extreme return.
feasibility_reason: The one-day large-stock effect (0.12%, close to close, pre-1997) is smaller than a round trip on a Rs 50,000 position. Useful as a watchlist input, not a standalone trade.

name: Delivery-volume change from the previous day
rule: DQ = deliverable quantity, DP = DQ/traded quantity. Accumulation flag: DQ>=2*mean(DQ,20) and DP>=mean(DP,20)+10 points and return>=+1%: next-day long watchlist. Distribution: same with return<=-1%: short watchlist. Froth: return>=+3% and DP<=mean(DP,20)-10 points: next-day fade. Enter on a 15-min opening-range break in the watchlist direction; stop 0.5*ATR14; exit 15:10.
instruments: NSE cash equities, intraday (MIS), long and short
holding_period: intraday on the day after the flag
reported_performance: No trading test found. Capitalmind, which publishes the data, says it is not very useful to trade on by itself; its January 2016 tables are descriptive. Small Granger-causality studies on a handful of NSE stocks give mixed results (2008-2018). Delivery percentage rises before NSE bulk deals (2010-2019).
feasibility_reason: Selection uses a free daily exchange file (deliverable quantity; must confirm we hold it) and trades go through cash MIS. Evidence is the weak point, not the account size.

name: Futures open-interest change with price change
rule: From the daily F&O file sum stock-futures OI over all expiries. dOI = OI/OI_prev-1; dP = futures close/prev-1. Long build-up: dP>=+1% and dOI>=+5%: next-day long watchlist. Short build-up: dP<=-1% and dOI>=+5%: short watchlist. Test short covering (dP up, dOI<=-5%) and long unwinding separately. Enter on a 15-min opening-range break; exit 15:10. Skip the last 3 sessions before expiry.
instruments: NSE cash equities of F&O underlyings, intraday (MIS), long and short
holding_period: intraday on the day after the signal
reported_performance: No test of next-day returns found for NSE stock futures. Broker and scanner sites publish the four labels daily without follow-up returns; the academic work located studies volatility, not direction (NSE 2005-2012).
feasibility_reason: Signals come from the free daily F&O file; trades are in cash, so futures lot sizes and margins do not matter.

name: Yesterday's top gainers and losers: reversal versus continuation
rule: At the close rank the universe by close-to-close return; G = top 5, L = bottom 5. Next session test (a) reversal: short G and buy L at the open, exit 15:10; (b) continuation: the opposite; (c) enter only on a 15-min opening-range break in the tested direction. Report splits by volume shock, results day and next-morning gap direction.
instruments: NSE cash equities, intraday (MIS), long and short
reported_performance: NSE 500, 2014-2021: the daily timescale shows the strongest reversal, a reversal portfolio made a 16-fold gross profit (abstract; costs not mentioned). US 1963-2015: stocks that were both top-80 daily winners and losers returned -1.07% the next month versus +0.53% for stocks that were neither. Monthly horizon in India shows continuation.
feasibility_reason: Ten positions of Rs 15,000 pay the 0.27% flat-fee floor each; cut to 2 per side. Intraday shorts are allowed in cash MIS. Published Indian result is before costs and assumes daily turnover.

name: Results day and the day after
rule: Day0 = first session a result is tradable. Pre-market result: apply the relative-volume opening-range rule to result stocks. Intraday result: when 5-min volume>5x its 20-day same-slot mean, enter in the bar's direction on a break of its extreme, stop at the other end. Day+1: trade Day0's direction only if Day0 closed in the top or bottom quarter of its range, entering on a 15-min opening-range break. Exit 15:10.
instruments: NSE cash equities, intraday (MIS), long and short
reported_performance: No intraday test found. India drift evidence conflicts: significant post-earnings drift 2002-2017 in one study; no exploitable drift in 100 NSE firms 2014-2018 in another. US 1984 study: price reacts within minutes, rule profits gone in 5-10 minutes, volatility stays elevated into the next day.
feasibility_reason: Trades are ordinary cash MIS positions. The constraint is data: we hold no results calendar with announcement times.

name: 52-week high proximity and breakout day
rule: near = close/max(high, 252 days). Watchlist: near>=0.97. Buy when price trades above the prior 252-day high and cumulative volume to that minute>=1.5x its 20-day same-minute mean. Stop 0.5*ATR14. Exit 15:10. Long only. Separate test: the day after a new 252-day low, buy on a break of the 15-min opening-range high.
instruments: NSE cash equities, long only (MIS)
reported_performance: US 1982-2006 (2,000 stocks): volume spikes when price crosses a 52-week extreme; next-week abnormal return about 0.6% after highs and about 5% after lows in the smallest quarter of stocks. 52-week-high momentum is profitable in 18 of 20 markets but not significant after costs in most. Weekly to monthly effects; no intraday evidence.
feasibility_reason: One or two long cash MIS positions. The documented effect is multi-day and concentrated in small stocks, so intraday benefit in the top 200 is doubtful.

name: F&O ban entry, exit and MWPL utilisation
rule: U = aggregate F&O open interest/MWPL from the exchange daily file. States: approaching (0.85<=U<0.95), ban day 1, in ban, exit day. (a) Exclude ban and approaching stocks from long strategies. (b) Ban day 1: short on a break of the 15-min opening-range low in cash. (c) Exit day: buy on a break of the 15-min range high. Stop 0.5*ATR14. Exit 15:10.
instruments: NSE cash equities of banned or near-ban F&O stocks, intraday (MIS)
reported_performance: NSE ban stocks Jan 2018-Sep 2022 (79 companies): average holding-period return over the ban was negative in the COVID and post-COVID periods; futures overnight volatility rose during bans. No trading rule tested. Forum anecdotes claim a rise after ban exit.
feasibility_reason: Cash intraday only; new futures or options positions in a banned stock are not allowed anyway. Needs the historical ban and MWPL file, and rules changed on 8 Dec 2025 (delta-based OI, new limit formula).

name: Price-band proximity
rule: Risk rule: for fixed-band stocks never short intraday within 2% of the upper band nor hold longs within 2% of the lower band; for F&O stocks treat a 9.9% move as a 15-minute halt and keep stop prices inside the current band. Test on daily data: after a close at the upper (lower) band, measure next-day open-to-close and close-to-close returns.
instruments: risk rule for NSE cash equities; daily test on fixed-band stocks
holding_period: not applicable (risk rule); daily test 1 day
reported_performance: NSE (2017 paper, abstract): cumulative abnormal returns of stocks hitting the upper band keep rising after the event day and volume stays high for 5 days; size not available. Magnet-effect evidence abroad is mixed.
feasibility_reason: Fixed-band stocks are illiquid and a locked circuit can trap the whole account in one position; our 200 liquid names are mostly F&O stocks with flexing bands, so this is mainly a safety rule.

name: Bulk and block deal catalyst
rule: Each evening read the exchange bulk and block deal file. Buy-only deals in stocks with minute data: next-day long watchlist, enter on a break of the 15-min opening-range high with RVOL5>=1.5, stop 0.5*ATR14, exit 15:10. Pre-deal signature test: 3-day rising volume and delivery percentage with positive abnormal return in mid caps.
instruments: NSE cash equities, long only (MIS)
holding_period: intraday on the day after the deal
reported_performance: NSE bulk deals 2010-2019: about 5-7% within a week around the deal for those positioned before it; volume and delivery percentage rise significantly before deals. The gain is pre-disclosure; nothing is shown for entries after the deal is published.
feasibility_reason: Most bulk-deal names are mid and small caps outside our 200-stock minute-data set, and the documented profit precedes public disclosure.

name: Pre-open auction gap and volume ranking
rule: At 09:08 read the pre-open indicative price and matched quantity per stock. gap_pre = indicative price/prev_close-1; pvol = matched quantity/20-day mean pre-open quantity. Rank by pvol and |gap_pre| to pre-select stocks for opening-range strategies. Proxy with held data: gap from the 09:15 open and first 1-minute volume relative to its 14-day mean.
instruments: ranking input for NSE cash equities
reported_performance: No predictive test found. The one study opened (India, auction introduced 18 Oct 2010) finds no significant effect of the auction on market quality.
feasibility_reason: Costs nothing to trade on, but we hold no pre-open snapshots; they would have to be recorded going forward. Only the proxy is testable now.

name: Intraday top movers at a fixed time: continuation versus reversal
rule: At T rank the universe by return since prev_close; M_up = top 5, M_down = bottom 5. Test (a) continuation to 15:10; (b) reversal over the next 30 and 60 minutes; (c) continuation only if cumulative volume>=2x its 14-day same-time mean; (d) reversal only if below 1x. Stop 0.5*ATR14.
instruments: NSE cash equities, intraday (MIS), long and short
reported_performance: No direct test. India (2015, abstract): returns reverse within minutes of extreme intraday moves, faster after falls. US: short-term reversal lasts under an hour and is tied to liquidity imbalance; index returns continue into the close; high opening volume favours continuation (2016-2023).
feasibility_reason: Short holding periods and up to ten small positions put the 0.13-0.27% round trip against moves of similar size; run with 2 per side at most.

name: Per-stock strategy fitness (walk-forward)
rule: For a base intraday strategy keep the per-stock trailing sum of R over the last 120 sessions (min 15 trades). Monthly, trade only stocks in the top third by this score. Validate walk-forward: compare next-month results of the top third versus the bottom third; drop the filter if the out-of-sample spread is not positive.
instruments: filter applied to NSE cash equities
reported_performance: In-sample only. US 2016-2023: best names for the 5-minute breakout made +309R to +385R (DDD, FSLR, NVDA), worst -128R to -154R, with no persistence test. NIFTY 50 paper (2024): per-stock rules work for some stocks, not all. No out-of-sample evidence that fitness persists.
feasibility_reason: A filter; no extra cost. High risk of fitting noise with under five years of minute data.
